title: Peak isometric axial twisting torque, standing, trunk pre-rotation -30°, cw effort, males
condition: maximal isometric axial twist cw, trunk pre-rotated -30°, standing with pelvis fixed

quantity.name: peak axial torque
quantity.definition: peak axial torque about the vertical Cybex axis during maximal isometric twisting; mean (SD) over subjects x 3 trials

source.sample: 15 subjects in Table 3 (10 M, 5 F); 11 M + 5 F in MVC-normalisation part; healthy university students, no LBP for >=1 year, in vivo

protocol.summary: Standing; pelvis fixed (ASIS rigid fixator + adjustable belt); upper-torso jig harness clamped at shoulder level (handles for arm position) connected through a ~0.6 m telescopic shaft with two universal joints to a Cybex II head mounted overhead with vertical axle: trunk free in all directions except axial rotation, so only axial torque about the vertical dynamometer axis is measured (no coupled moments recorded). 3 trials per condition, slow build-up to peak at ~4 s.
how_to_simulate: Upright standing, pelvis fixed; thorax rotated -30° relative to the pelvis (0 = neutral).
Apply a pure axial torque to the thorax at shoulder level (cw); no restraint of flexion/lateral bending (universal joints).
Compare model maximal axial torque (or required max muscle stress) with data; the model's coupled moments should be ~0 externally (free harness).
protocol.notes: Direction naming: cw/ccw as printed. From the right-side muscle pattern (right IO and latissimus agonists in cw, right EO agonist in ccw), cw corresponds to twisting the trunk to the right (right axial rotation) - inferred, not stated. '+30°' = trunk pre-rotated in the cw direction (Table 3 footnote). SD pooled across 3 trials per subject (n obs = 30 M / 15 F).
